title: Responsive component patterns
learningObjectives: Explain responsive component patterns and apply it to responsive components.

understand.concept: Responsive component patterns include wrapping navigation, fluid card grids, flexible media objects, content-led sidebars, and container-aware components. Patterns should adapt to available space without changing the meaning or logical reading order of content.
understand.whyItMatters: A component may appear in multiple contexts and languages. Test long labels, text enlargement, and different container widths rather than only checking a single desktop layout.
understand.analogy: A reusable component is a small adaptable tool that should fit more than one workspace.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; media and container queries use formal CSS conditions and sizing references.

explain.narrative: The grid automatically fits as many cards as the available width allows while respecting a minimum track size.

examples.explanation: The grid automatically fits as many cards as the available width allows while respecting a minimum track size.
examples.expectedOutput: A responsive example that changes based on viewport or container conditions.

practise.guidedTask: Build a reusable card that works in a narrow sidebar and a wide main column. Test long translated headings.
practise.independentTask: Build a reusable component and test it at different viewport and container sizes, with long labels and text enlargement.
hints: Inspect the actual query condition and container.
Test just below and above thresholds.
Keep content and keyboard order logical.

questions.prompt: What should a responsive reusable component adapt to?
options: Its available container space and content
questions.answer: Its available container space and content
questions.explanation: Responsive components should respond to their own available space and actual content.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable responsive test?
options: Test different widths and content lengths
Test only at one standard phone size
questions.answer: Test different widths and content lengths
questions.explanation: Responsive behaviour depends on actual space and content, not just a device label.
